workstream: qgraph vertex index (VGraph) search path and stored encoding: 4-bit traversal codes, 4-bit residual, cache-line-aligned rows, BFS vertex reordering, 3-byte neighbour ids, heap pool, inlined SDOT, split scales, u8 visited epochs, next-adjacency prefetch
method: public-bench ann-qgraph --index vertex --holdout 2000 (held-out train vectors, exact cosine truth; test.f32 and neighbors.i32 not read). Graphs: nytimes-256-angular degree 64, glove-100-angular degree 32, build_ef 200, alpha 1.0, seed 24301, built once by the baseline binary and loaded from a graph cache (--graph-cache) by every process; the cached graphs reproduce the committed untimed sweeps exactly (all 65 rows, recall and evals). Timing: one process per encoding started with --sync, all built and ready outside the lock, then one coordinator under /Volumes/A/.hms-target/timed.sh rotates the processes round by round (round r starts with process r mod N), single-threaded search, 2,000 queries per config per round; load recorded before every step.
selection_rule: Per process and threshold: the qualifying row (recall >= threshold) with the fewest code estimates per query (deterministic, not chosen by noisy QPS). Paired ratio per round = candidate QPS / A QPS in the same round; median and all rounds reported.

process_legend.A: baseline binary (integrate/qgraph-speed 4ed59b8 search code + graph cache), --residual (8-bit code, 8-bit residual)
process_legend.E (round 1 only): new code, default flags (same encoding as A; heap pool, inlined SDOT, split scales, u8 epochs, adjacency prefetch)

identity_checks: Recall is deterministic: F == B row for row on both datasets (3-byte ids change no result); B, C, D identical across rounds where configs overlap; new code with default flags differs from A only by tie order among duplicate vectors (+0.0000..+0.0015 recall, +0..+4 evals/query on nytimes; identical on glove); re-rank ties break by original id so reordering changes no recall beyond that.

caveats: Machine load (1-minute) was 160-270 during the round-1/2 windows (glove1, ny1, glove2, ny2) and lower in glove3 and ny3 (see load_1m_per_step), against ~7 for the committed before-numbers: absolute QPS here is 3-6x below the committed values and per-round ratios scatter widely (0.8-3.4). Only paired ratios are meaningful; anchored_qps = median ratio x committed QPS at the same baseline params is an extrapolation across that load difference, not a measurement.
Bandwidth-saving encodings (4-bit codes, 3-byte ids, alignment) may gain more under memory contention than on an idle machine.
This agent's cargo build overlapped the first ~45 s of the ny1 window.
Another agent's timed runs held the lock between windows; windows never overlapped (flock).

The new-code default path (E) showed no gain on nytimes (median 0.94 at 0.90, 1.06 at 0.95) and +8-9% on glove in round 1: inconclusive at this noise level; the defaults keep the same encoding but run the new pool/kernel code.

conclusion.recommended_encoding: --residual --vertex-bits 4 --residual-bits 8 --align-rows --reorder --id-bytes 3 (process D in round 2, ny3, glove4); rerank 32 (nytimes) / 64 (glove). Not made the default: defaults keep the committed 8-bit/8-bit encoding (flags off).

conclusion.smallest_memory_measured: glove H (--residual-bits 4 --reorder --id-bytes 3, 8-bit traversal): 331,263,724 bytes (-23%), paired 1.145-1.364 at 0.90 and 1.121-1.434 at 0.95; nytimes 4-bit traversal with 4-bit residual (152,167,984 bytes, -32%) loses ~0.005 recall at equal ef (untimed only).
conclusion.what_moved_qps: Reordering is the largest single gain (glove G 1.30-1.55, nytimes G 1.25-1.33); 4-bit traversal codes add speed on nytimes (256-d rows halve to one 128-byte line) and memory on both; cache-line alignment of 8-bit glove rows is inconclusive (step time H/C 1.052 in glove3, 0.981 in glove4) for +19 MB and does not apply to the recommended encoding's 64-byte glove / 128-byte nytimes rows; 3-byte ids change no result and no measurable speed (B vs F within noise) for -18.6 MB / -37.8 MB.
negative_or_inconclusive: new pool/kernel code at default flags (E): 0.94 / 1.06 on nytimes, 1.08 / 1.09 on glove under load 175-270: no demonstrated gain
4-bit residual with 8-bit traversal (C) is not faster than 8/8 on nytimes (0.96-1.40)
4-bit traversal with 4-bit residual: -0.005 recall at equal ef on nytimes, not timed
